newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi urges Italy left to start pension talks.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi urges Italy left to start pension talks.

text.p: Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi on Tuesday urged the head of the largest party in Italy's ruling centre-left coalition to forge ahead with reforming the pension system.

Berlusconi, writing in Rome daily Il Messagero, called on Massimo D'Alema, leader of the former communist Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), not to listen to "sirens" in trade unions and the hard-left Communist Refoundation party.
"We are and remain ready to review pensions spending as soon as possible without devastating the welfare state," former prime minister Berlusconi wrote.
Communist Refoundation, led by Fausto Bertinotti, lends vital support to Prime Minister Romano Prodi in parliament but has vowed to bring down the government if social spending is cut.

Italy carried out some pension reforms in 1995 but the government wants to revise the system once more and Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said earlier this week some adjustment to pensions spending was "probable" and as far as he was concerned, the sooner it happened the better.
But unions, backed by Communist Refoundation, have fiercely opposed moves to bring forward debate on the 1995 deal which was originally scheduled to begin in 1998.
The PDS draws a great deal of its support from the unions and D'Alema on Monday called for a full debate to be held with union leaders on the whole welfare state.

But Berlusconi, writing in Il Messagero, said: "From his words, it is not clear whether or not (D'Alema) agrees with us and, if we are not wrong, with the Treasury Minister of the government which the PDS supports."
He called Communist Refoundation and the trade unions "sirens" to whom D'Alema must listen.

"Tie yourself to the ship's mast and explain to the honourable Bertinotti and (CGIL trade union federation leader) Sergio Cofferati that the injustices, the privileges and the incongruities of our pension system must be modified in the interests of everyone," he wrote.

Welfare state reform has become a pressing issue as Italy tries to bring its state finances into line in order to meet economic criteria to be among founding members of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
However Bertinotti, interviewed in La Repubblica newspaper, repeated his stance. "If the PDS leader is thinking of reducing the level of safeguards on pensions, there will be a hard political clash."
